title: Now and before verb match
subject: Arabic
unit: Summer 1: My grandparents and relatives; the market; Ramadan and Eid
source: Seeded from arabic/y3 lesson 17 (Pupil PDF worksheet: now and before verb match)
intro: Lesson 17: Verbs in the past tense: ذَهَبْتُ، أَكَلْتُ. To understand how to say what I did in the past with verbs ending in ـتُ

questions.model: Teacher: أَلْعَبُ is 'I play' now. For the past, take لَعِبَ (he played) and add ـتُ: لَعِبْتُ, 'I played'.

questions.q: On the pupil PDF, match four present verbs to their past forms, then write two sentences starting with أَمْسِ about what you did yesterday.
questions.a: Matches: أَذْهَبُ ذَهَبْتُ، آكُلُ أَكَلْتُ، أَشْرَبُ شَرِبْتُ، أَلْعَبُ لَعِبْتُ; two correct sentences
questions.model: Teacher writes: أَمْسِ شَرِبْتُ حَلِيبًا (yesterday I drank milk).

questions.q: write 'I read' in the past: قَرَأْتُ.
tell your partner three things you did at Eid in the past tense.
questions.a: For example: ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى المَسْجِدِ، أَكَلْتُ، لَعِبْتُ

questions.q: Back to our ponder: how does Arabic show the past?
questions.a: It changes the verb; with 'I' it ends in ـتُ
